items.title: fix: Incorrect accuracy tracking when quiz passes score
items.body:
Fixed quizProgress.js accuracy tracking when quizzes call recordAttempt() with score that is not a plain correct-answer count.

What changed
recordAttempt() previously did: correct = typeof correctCount === "number" ? correctCount : got;
If correctCount was missing and score was a percent/ratio/points value, it incorrectly treated score as “number of correct answers”.
Now it computes correct for analytics as follows:
Use correctCount when it’s a finite number.
If correctCount is missing, infer correctness only when score looks like an accuracy metric:
ratio form: 0..1 → correct = round(score * totalQuestions)
percent form: >1..100 → correct = round((score/100) * totalQuestions)
Otherwise, set correct = null so we do not update correctTotal / chart accuracy for that attempt.


closes #79

## Intent

Deliver PR 3 for FE Arena to improve learning feedback and current-run practice guidance without adding accounts, difficulty-aware gameplay, or production hardening. After each round, use a server-authoritative reveal period lasting up to 30 seconds so both players can review the answer, explanation, assumptions, provenance, and relevant reasoning, with a visible per-seat skip; both skips advance immediately, one skip leaves the other review time available until expiry or the other skip. Make reveal deadlines, skip state, reconnect behavior, late requests, duplicate skips, forfeits, abandoned matches, and solo practice deterministic and server-authoritative. Never expose answers or explanations before reveal/results, including graph and C questions. Prevent repeated questions within private, public, and solo runs, including Supabase-loaded banks, and fail safely when a unique run cannot be filled. Show current-run per-topic attempted/correct/incorrect/accuracy plus useful score/timing context, and provide lightweight missed/weak-topic guidance with a clear account-free solo practice action for a selected topic without persisting raw answers. Strengthen post-question explanations for all six supported types, including graph/C-specific reasoning, while keeping them hidden early. Update stale copy to six answer types. Preserve scoring, rematches, chat, room isolation, Supabase terminal-summary persistence, guest-first behavior, current-run privacy, Socket.IO transport, no migrations/credentials, no accounts/auth, no difficulty-aware gameplay, no arbitrary code execution, and no raw-answer persistence.

- Added current-run topic metrics, score/timing context, missed-topic guidance, selected-topic account-free solo practice, and updated six-answer-type copy and documentation.

✅ Low: The latest fix consistently counts timed-out match seats in topic summaries, and the branch now satisfies the reviewed reveal, privacy, deadline, reconnect, deduplication, and solo-feedback requirements without a remaining material issue.

items.title: MathQuest v0.11.0: Home Assistant dashboard statistics
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a stable, dashboard-focused Home Assistant statistics interface backed by MathQuest's real learner data.

## Home Assistant API
- Adds authenticated `GET /api/ha/stats` for full dashboard statistics.
- Adds authenticated `GET /api/ha/summary` for lightweight 30–60 second polling.
- Exposes questions/correct/incorrect/accuracy today, hints, completed activities, streak, daily and total XP, recommended topic and last activity.
- Adds Number, Measurement, Space, Algebra and Probability category data with progress, accuracy, questions and mastery.
- Adds rolling seven-day questions, accuracy, hints, activities and XP.
- Returns null for genuinely missing optional data without failing the rest of the payload.
- Returns a stable relative `app_path` and deliberately avoids hard-coding HA ingress tokens/routes.

## Architecture
- Reuses the existing v0.6 adaptive topic metrics and mastery weighting rather than creating duplicate learning-statistics logic.
- Keeps v0.10 and all prior learning behaviour intact.
- Direct native HA entity registration is not appropriate for the current ingress add-on architecture, so README documentation provides REST sensor configuration instead.

## Home Assistant documentation
- Adds a `Home Assistant Dashboard Integration` README section.
- Includes endpoint/authentication details, example JSON, REST sensor YAML, units, timestamp device class guidance, 30–60 second refresh guidance and an example dashboard card.
- Home Assistant REST entities naturally become unavailable when MathQuest cannot be reached.

## Tests and validation
- Adds backend regression coverage for zero activity, accuracy calculations, category statistics, hint updates, activity/last-activity updates, missing optional data and compact summary output.
- CI now runs pytest in addition to Python compilation.
- Existing TypeScript/Vite and Home Assistant metadata validation remain required.

## Release
- Bumps runtime, frontend and Home Assistant add-on metadata to v0.11.0.
- Updates changelog.

items.title: Fix label shape crash in train_model + add image size check
items.body:
## Błąd

Uruchomienie w Colabie (`00c6605`) padło na Sekcji 7 (Baseline) z:
```
RuntimeError: 0D or 1D target tensor expected, multi-target not supported
```

## Przyczyna

`PneumoniaMNIST` (MedMNIST) zwraca etykiety w kształcie `(batch, 1)`, nie `(batch,)`. `evaluate_model()` i `get_roc_data()` miały już `.reshape(-1)` na etykietach, ale `train_model()` — funkcja faktycznie trenująca model — tego nie robiła:
- `criterion(outputs, labels)` dostawał `(batch, 1)` zamiast `(batch,)` → crash w `CrossEntropyLoss`
- `(preds == labels).sum()` z kształtami `(batch,)` vs `(batch,1)` broadcastowałoby się do macierzy `(batch,batch)` — cichy błąd, który zawyżałby accuracy (dopiero po naprawieniu pierwszego problemu)

## Zmiany

- `train_model()`: `labels.to(device)` → `labels.reshape(-1).to(device)` — naprawia oba problemy jedną zmianą, ten sam wzorzec co w `evaluate_model`/`get_roc_data`
- Nowa komórka po sekcji ładowania danych: wypisuje surowy rozmiar obrazu z MedMNIST oraz kształt tensora wchodzącego do sieci — potwierdzenie, że obrazy są natywnie 224×224 (nie skalowane z 28×28)
- Wyczyszczony nieaktualny output błędu z komórki Baseline (do ponownego uruchomienia w Colabie)

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01GvwKxRPmCWTM3aQzrnXoGQ)_

Fix training crash caused by MedMNIST label shape and add a sanity check cell for image and tensor sizes in the experiment notebook.

- Ensure labels from PneumoniaMNIST are reshaped to 1D in the training loop to avoid CrossEntropyLoss runtime errors and incorrect accuracy computation.

items.title: fix(eval): correct benchmark execution semantics
items.body:
### Motivation

- The previous benchmark aborted the entire suite on a single malformed stage output and reported misleading schema/compliance and category metrics. 
- The judge contract used by the benchmark deviated from the compact production `JudgeVerdict` + trusted materialization path, enabling silent repairs and invalid evidence acceptance. 
- Important-finding probe matching was conflated with semantic finding-category accuracy, producing incorrect category accuracy numbers. 
- The benchmark must preserve BlindGuard semantics and record per-case typed failures so real Codex-native runs can be trusted and audited.

### Description

- Execute every case independently and record per-case stage outcomes without aborting the suite, introducing `StageStatus` and typed `FailureCategory` to classify forward/verifier/judge/evidence/orchestration/provider failures. 
- Request the compact `JudgeVerdict` contract from the judge and materialize it with `materialize_judge_verdict(...)`, failing closed on invalid evidence rather than normalizing or repairing malformed output. 
- Replace hard-coded schema-compliance metrics with derived rates computed from actual stage attempts and successful decodes, and separate important-finding text-probe detection from true finding-category accuracy by comparing the trusted persisted verdict categories. 
- Add suite metadata (suite hash, git revision, generated timestamp), per-case execution_mode, and persist a deterministic 40-case report artifact (path: `reports/benchmark-v1/deterministic.json`); update `fixtures/evaluation/cases.json`, tests, and docs to reflect the honest execution semantics.

### Testing

- Ran formatting and lint gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, which passed. 
- Ran unit and integration tests and deterministic evaluation: `cargo test --workspace` and focused CLI tests (`cargo test -p flect-cli --test evaluation` and `cargo test -p flect-cli --bin flect eval::tests`), which passed; added new eval unit tests covering typed schema failures and closed evidence-validation failures. 
- Executed the deterministic 40-case offline run (`cargo run -p flect-cli -- eval --output reports/benchmark-v1/deterministic.json`), producing the persistent report artifact with 40 attempted / 40 persisted / 0 failed fixture cases (deterministic plumbing only). 
- One environment-specific issue remains: several `flect-runner` HTTP/Responses integration tests that expect proxied/mock network behavior failed in this runtime because provider HTTP interactions were intercepted and returned authentication responses; this indicates the current environment cannot reliably simulate the provider network surface or spawn fresh Codex verifier/judge agents, so no real Codex-native 40-case run was performed and no live-model performance claims are made.

items.title: fix(metrics): stop impossible results being computed and persisted
items.body:
Ten defects where the *number* was wrong. Each was reproduced as a failing test before being fixed.

## Measured, before → after

| Defect | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| AFK burst, Time/30, 3 keys in 100 ms | `NetWPM=360.0`, persisted, became a personal best | `NetWPM=0`, `AFKTrimmed=true`, not stored, not ranked |
| Zero duration, one wrong key | `Accuracy=100.0`, `KeystrokeAccuracy=100.0` | `0.0 / 0.0` |
| Strict `abcdef` replay desync (engine buffer really is `abcdef`) | `Correct=9 Incorrect=2 Accuracy=81.82` | `Correct=6 Incorrect=0 Accuracy=100.00` |
| Strict, keys past end of target | buffer `abzzzzzzzzzz`, `Extra=10` | buffer `ab`, `Extra=0` |
| `Progress()` | Time `0/30000` (milliseconds as a word count), Code `0/0` | Time `0/3` words, Code `0/5` runes |
| Consistency, even 5 c/s over 3.2 s | `60.08` | `76.16` (the formula maximum) |

`knownImplausible` is now **empty** and the ratchet passes with zero entries.

## Two user-visible behaviour changes

- **Consistency scores rise for everyone.** The final partial second was scaled as if it were whole. A perfectly even typist could not score the formula maximum. Scores only move up; stored history is untouched.
- **A run abandoned mid-test is no longer saved,** and says so rather than vanishing. Its rates describe the burst typed before walking away, so a stored record would stand as a personal best nobody could beat by typing.
- Strict-mode `Errors` now counts **every** wrong key including corrected ones, per the recorded decision — the same run reports `5` where it used to report `2`.

## The assertion whose absence let this ship

The AFK defect spanned `TrimAFK → Compute → Record.NetWPM → IsNewBest → AppendHistory` — four packages — and every existing test was within-package. `internal/app/result_persistence_test.go` is the cross-package seam: it runs an AFK-shaped result through `handleResultMsg` and asserts nothing was persisted and no best was recorded.

Verified independently before merge: forcing `AFKTrimmed` to false fails all three `internal/app` seam tests plus two in `internal/metrics`.

## `typedFromLog` was a second copy of the same bug

`internal/ui/typing_log_helpers.go` reimplemented the buggy replay loop byte-for-byte, so fixing `compute.go` alone would have left it. Collapsed rather than fixed twice: `typing.ReplayBuffer`/`typing.TypedFromLog` is now the single definition and both callers delegate.

`typing.Keystroke` gained `Blocked` with `omitempty`, so pre-existing replay logs decode to `false` — today's behaviour. Covered by a fixture written without the field.

`engine.go` split 197 → 156 across `engine_states.go`, `engine_progress.go`, `replay.go`. `Engine.wordTarget` renamed to `Engine.limit`: the old name asserted a unit that is wrong in Time mode, which was the `Progress()` bug.

12 mutations run, 12 caught.

## Two deviations from the phase spec, both forced by file ownership

1. **`EligibleForBest` gained no AFK branch.** `storage.Record` has no AFK field and that file was owned by a concurrent phase. Since AFK runs are never written, no stored record can carry the flag; the gate lives in `app.decideOutcome`, the only writer, enforced by the seam tests.
2. **The notice never lengthens an already-overflowing frame.** Inserting unconditionally would have changed a `knownAppOverflow` entry from 29 to 30 lines in a file this phase must not edit. Every other measurement is byte-identical, and the insert path activates for free once the Result screen comes inside 24 rows.

## Open

Consistency for sub-one-second runs is now 0. Unreachable in practice, but it is a new value, not an inherited one.

items.title: Add username/password auth, comprehensive event logging + debug panel, progress dashboard, and a verify-hang fix
items.body:
## Summary

This branch adds **username/password auth** and a **comprehensive, structured event-logging + observability layer** to the Regenerate-Until-Valid pipeline, plus a **progress dashboard** and a fix for a real-provider verification hang. It builds on the session-based flowchart work already on the branch.

The verifier remains the oracle; none of this changes the acceptance rule or the six failure codes. All additions keep the offline `mock` path green.

## What's included

**Auth**
- Username/password login with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashing (stdlib, offline); `password_hash` excluded from every API response.
- **Forgot / reset password** (token-based). No mail server in this app, so `/auth/forgot-password` issues a short-lived (30 min), single-use token and returns it directly (dev delivery, labeled as such in the UI); only the token's hash is stored. `/auth/reset-password` consumes a valid, unexpired token and signs the user in. Generic response for unknown users (no enumeration).

**Comprehensive per-user + per-session event log**
- Every action is one immutable `Event` row keyed by both the user (`student_id`) and the login session (`session_id`).
- The full regenerate-until-valid trace is logged: `generate_start → candidate → verify_start → verify_step (per sub-check, with ms timing + mode) → accept | reject → deliver`, plus `exhausted`. Failed attempts are captured with phase (parse/contract/verify) and full failure detail.
- **GUI actions** are logged too (`ui` events): logins, settings changes, next/adaptive clicks, submit, solution toggle, debug toggles, stats open.
- Retrieval: `GET /students/{id}/events` (all sessions) or `?session_id=` (one session).

**Frontend Debug panel**
- Toggle-on right-half panel showing the live log (polls every 3s), color-coded by type, with a this-session / all-sessions scope switch.
- The practice screen no longer exposes failed regeneration attempts — they live only in the Debug panel. A neutral spinner with a live elapsed-seconds counter replaces the old inline trace.
- Opt-in **"log prompt"** captures the full LLM prompt into `generate_start` (collapsible in the panel; off by default since prompts are ~1.9 KB).
- Timestamps render as full local date + time.

**Verify hang fix + clarity-check control**
- Root cause: the semantic clarity check makes a *second* LLM call per candidate, and the OpenAI/Gemini client had no timeout, so a stalled/rate-limited call (common on Gemini's free tier) blocked up to ~600s. Added `LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60) + `LLM_MAX_RETRIES` (2); the semantic check now degrades gracefully on a network error.
- New `SEMANTIC_LLM_CHECK` (default true) + a Debug "⚙ Advanced" toggle to run clarity via the offline heuristic instead of a 2nd LLM call.

**Progress dashboard**
- New `GET /students/{id}/stats` aggregates the log + delivered problems into per-user totals (sessions, solved, attempts, correct/incorrect, accuracy, time spent) and per-skill mastery + difficulty progression.
- A "📊 Progress" screen with summary cards, a per-skill table (mastery bar + difficulty-over-time sparkline), and a count of untouched skills.

## Notes for reviewers
- **SQLite migration:** `Student` gained `reset_token_hash` + `reset_expires_at`; `db.init_db()` adds these columns in place on an existing `stemgen.db` (SQLModel's `create_all` never ALTERs), so no data loss and no manual migration. Postgres deployments should use real migrations.
- **"Time spent"** is the sum of each login session's first-to-last event span (engaged time), not wall-clock since signup.
- Event `type` values expanded (e.g. `fail` → structured `reject`); the log is still append-only and the six failure codes are unchanged.
- `CONFIG.md` documents the three new env vars.
- 62 tests pass, fully offline on the mock provider; frontend type-checks clean.

items.title: Running 0–5 scoring, single-word feed filter, and health check
items.body:
## Summary
Replaces the *retire-after-5-correct* rule with a **running per-word score in [0, 5]**, adds a **Health check** report, filters the feed to single words, and moves the cron schedules off the top of the hour. Scoring lives on the 🤔-flagged quiz pool (`data/review/words.json`).

## Scoring model (`scoring.py`)
- Correct quiz answer → `+1` (cap 5); incorrect → `-1` (floor 0); 🤔 tap → reset to 0.
- `learned` = `score == 5` (leaves the quiz pool); `in_review` = pooled (`drained`) and not learned; `correct`/`incorrect` kept as lifetime totals.
- Legacy `retired` records are migrated to `learned` automatically (score seeded from `retired`/`correct−incorrect`).

## Changes
- **`drain_updates.py`** — a 🤔 tap resets the word's score and (re)adds it to the pool; poll answers move the score. Updates processed in `update_id` order so the running score is deterministic.
- **`send_quiz.py`** — quizzes in-review (not-learned) words; increments a per-word `quizzes` counter.
- **`send_word.py`** — rejects multi-word phrases and skips learned words.
- **`health_check.py` + `health.yml`** — per-word table (Score, Learned, In review, Checks, Quizzes, Correct/Incorrect, Accuracy, 🤔 clicks, Drained, Last seen) to the Actions step summary; runs on demand or daily.
- **`vocab.yml` / `quiz.yml`** — cron moved off `:00` (`17 …` and `7 4 …`); GitHub drops/delays top-of-hour runs, which is why the 9 PM quiz was arriving ~1–2 AM.

## Verification
Verified locally against the real data repo: scoring state machine (clamp/reset/learned/back-to-review), legacy `retired` migration, drain end-to-end with mocked Telegram updates, `send_quiz` selection + quiz counter + poll registration, feed filter (no multi-word/learned leaks), and report rendering.

## Notes / decisions
- **`learned` is dynamic** (`score == 5`), not a permanent latch — a 🤔 tap on a learned word resets it to 0 and returns it to review. This is the alternative flagged in planning; say the word if you'd rather it latch permanently.
- The `quizzes` counter is forward-only (historical quiz sends weren't recorded), so existing words show `quizzes: 0` until their next quiz.

items.title: Preserve prompt ordering in batch inference responses
items.body:
**Problem**
When evaluating more than 128 prompts, the inference client switches to an upload-based path (upload_generate + poll_for_downloads). The server returns results as a dict keyed by {job_hash}_{index}. The original code iterated over this dict without sorting, so responses were matched to the wrong prompts — making the model appear to generate completely incorrect outputs for large eval sets.

**Fix**
Sort the results dict by the numeric suffix of each key before converting to a list, restoring the original prompt submission order.

**Impact**
No effect on runs with ≤128 prompts (different code path)
Fixes incorrect accuracy measurements on any eval set >128 examples

These changes enhance hardware compatibility, precision of configuration, diagnostic capabilities, and development ergonomics.

items.title: feat(retag): add color-scheme calibration packet
items.body:
## What this adds

A human calibration harness for the deterministic `colorScheme` detector, and the first calibration result it produced.

- Deterministic 12-row cohort selection from the immutable color-scheme audit, re-derivable by any verifier.
- Hash-bound Zod contracts for packets, submissions, and calibration reports.
- Standalone DM Sans reviewer HTML with screenshot evidence, light/dark/abstain controls, required abstention reasons, per-reviewer drafts, import, copy, and download.
- CLI for private packet generation and evaluation; it refuses corpus output paths, existing outputs, stale image hashes, and corpus mutation.
- Documentation that makes calibration a prerequisite for promotion.

**Corpus bytes are unchanged by every command here.** No gold labels, submission, or report file enters the repository.

## The calibration result: the detector failed

The harness was run for real against all 787 corpus entries. That is the headline of this PR, not the plumbing.

Packet `1110270c94eb4f686e7393427a97b9f5a6ebc97ad8a2df124be9bd1f1d439ce4`, audit `cd6c2ac5106224a0b4bd2e6730e9355e45227982ff76152dc2e78d38bbde13bc`, reviewer `Gold`, 12 rows:

```
selected=12 scored=12 correct=9 incorrect=3 abstained=0 accuracy=0.75
status: fail    promotionEligible: false
```

**All three disagreements were detector errors, reviewed against the screenshots — not reviewer errors.** `colorScheme` fill from `color-scheme-v1` is blocked pending a redesigned estimator. Two distinct failure modes:

- **Content, not chrome.** Two light-mode iOS screens — white nav, white product card, indigo primary button — each carry a near-black photographic modal covering most of the frame. Median luma **0.00** and **1.21**, classified `dark`. A whole-frame median tracks the dominant pixels; `colorScheme` is meant to describe the canvas and surface theme. Not an alpha artifact: those PNGs carry alpha, but flattening on white or on black yields identical luma, so the black pixels are opaque.
- **Chromatic background, not dark neutral.** A page of white text on saturated blue measured **91.35** and classified `dark`. Luma alone cannot separate a dark neutral canvas from a vivid hue.

Both modes fell **outside** the abstention band (`|luma - 110| < 12`, so 98–122), meaning the detector was confident and wrong rather than uncertain. The audit abstained **zero** times across all 787 entries, which now reads as a warning rather than a strength.

**That run also cannot speak to dark detection.** Every gold label was `light`, so the confusion matrix reads `expectedLight {light: 9, dark: 3}, expectedDark {light: 0, dark: 0}`. A single-class packet carries no evidence about the other class, and a *passing* run of the same shape would have been equally uninformative. Cohort strata derive from detector luma and cannot guarantee human-confirmed dark rows, so judging a replacement estimator needs gold labels in both classes.

The three named entries are now label-contaminated and must be excluded from future blind packets. They stay useful as regression cases.

This is the outcome the program's "never promote directly from detector output" rule exists for. The gate blocked promotion on its first real use.

## Review remediation (commits 6–8)

A review of the first five commits found three ways a calibration artifact could claim more than it proved.

**The cohort was self-attested.** `selectionSha256` was computed by hashing the cohort the packet carried and verified by hashing the same field, so any audit-consistent subset passed once both hashes were recomputed. Demonstrated with a packet holding only the four unambiguous rows of an eight-row audit, both threshold-near rows dropped and every stratum relabelled: it evaluated to `pass` at accuracy 1. `evaluate` now re-derives the cohort with `selectColorSchemeCalibrationEntries` and requires an exact match.

**The report was forgeable.** It named `submissionArtifactId` but carried no submission digest, `decisions` had no minimum length, and neither the confusion cells nor `status` were reconciled against `counts`. A hand-authored report with twelve correct counts, empty `decisions`, an all-zero confusion matrix and a submission ID that never existed validated as `pass`. The report now records `submissionSha256`, requires `decisions` to cover exactly the selected rows without duplicates, requires the confusion cells to sum to `scored` with the diagonal equal to `correct`, and derives `status` in all three branches.

**The reviewer page shipped the answer key it told reviewers to ignore.** `existingColorScheme`, `detectedColorScheme` and `medianLuma` were embedded in the page's `DATA`, reachable from View Source, two lines below a banner instructing reviewers to judge the screenshot and not the corpus value or the detector's prediction. Those three fields are no longer sent to the page.

**Gate thresholds are now auditable.** `--minimum-labels 1 --minimum-accuracy 0` still computes a real `pass`, so the report carries `promotionEligible`, derived against a fixed floor of 12 scored labels at accuracy 1. Promotion reads that field, not `status`.

**One canonical serialisation.** Digests previously hashed compact JSON while the CLI wrote pretty-printed JSON, and `auditSha256` hashed raw file bytes on a third convention. `sha256sum packet.json` now reproduces the recorded digest.

Also fixed: `evaluate` recomputes the audit digest from the audit it was handed rather than trusting a caller-supplied string; cohort tie-breaks compare by UTF-16 code unit instead of `localeCompare`, which made selection depend on host locale and ICU version; entry IDs are no longer interpolated into CSS selectors or used as plain object keys; a corrupt or partial stored draft degrades to blanks instead of leaving an inert page with no handlers attached; the Google Fonts request is gone, so the page issues no network request; output containment is re-checked after `mkdirSync`, immediately before the write.

**Reviewer-page regression, caught in real use and fixed in commit 8.** Per-reviewer drafts initially loaded the stored draft for whatever ID was being typed, so a reviewer who labeled all twelve rows and *then* entered their reviewer ID had every label replaced with blanks — and because `oninput` fires per keystroke, every prefix of the ID wiped again. Copy JSON and Download JSON then correctly refused to export an empty submission, so both buttons appeared dead. A stored draft is now adopted only when that reviewer actually has one. Two export defects surfaced while confirming it: the download anchor was never attached to the document and its blob URL was revoked on the same tick as the click, either of which cancels the download in a real browser; and with both the clipboard API and `execCommand` unavailable, which is routine for a `file://` page, a reviewer had no way to extract their labels at all. Both export paths now fall back to a visible, pre-selected textarea.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:contracts` clean.
- Full suite: **3967 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed**.
- Focused calibration tests: 9 → **35**. The 26 added were each written failing first, and include the cherry-picked cohort and the forged report as executable exploits, plus the CLI refusals Task 3 of the plan specified but never tested.
- Real corpus audit: 787 entries, 765 proposed, 22 unchanged, 0 conflicts, 0 abstained, 0 missing, 0 errors.
- End-to-end packet run: 12 rows stratified 4/4/4, all 12 image URLs resolve and re-hash to the recorded `imageSha256`, `sha256sum packet.json` matches the digest embedded in the page, page contains none of the three withheld fields and issues no network request.
- Corpus SHA-256 identical before and after every command (`c3fbc43225526a6104da8c3ebba484b84500921eda38c6b3ff97fc720ce958d0`).
- Selection determinism confirmed by generating the packet twice from the same audit: byte-identical JSON.

## Known remaining, not addressed here

- The report's `correct` / `incorrect` / `accuracy` fields read as grading the reviewer, when the reviewer is ground truth and the detector is under test. Better names would be `agreed` / `disagreed` / `detectorAgreement`.
- The `stratum` pill still tells a reviewer whether a row is threshold-near or a luma tail, which leaks difficulty though not the answer. The 12-label floor resists abstain-shopping.
- A reviewer can import a detector-generated submission and re-export it under their own ID; the submission envelope records no provenance distinguishing typed labels from imported ones.
- Output containment is re-checked immediately before the write, which narrows rather than closes the symlink-swap window; closing it needs `openat`-style APIs Node does not expose.
- Screenshots are referenced by absolute `file://` URL, so a packet is not portable between machines.
- Report `schemaVersion` stays `"1.0"` despite the added required fields. No calibration artifacts exist outside the scratchpad, so there is nothing to migrate.

Any packet generated before commit 6 is invalid: `selectionSha256` and `packetSha256` now have different values. Regenerate before labeling.

---

## Review outcome

Reviewed with `/review`, `/plan-eng-review` and `/plan-ceo-review`, plus three independent outside-voice passes. Landed in five commits after the original five.

**The finding that reframed the PR.** `color-scheme-v1` was already the sole authority for `colorScheme` on every newly tagged entry (`tagger.ts:2991`, overwriting the vision model's answer), so a harness gating a 765-row migration left the measured detector writing in production. Worse, `decision-lab.ts` lists `colorScheme` in `CITABLE_EXTRACTION_KEYS` and performs no `isVerified` check, so that answer was cited into synthesis prompts with no verification gate. `552d4b8` removes the stamp; the detection is still recorded in the run report as evidence.

**The calibration result, stated correctly.** The run ranks; it does not verdict. Every gold label was `light`, so the trivial baseline `return "light"` scores 12/12 against the detector's 9/12. Twelve rows stratified toward the hardest cases give a Wilson 95% interval of roughly 0.47-0.92 and carry no dark-class labels, so the run cannot establish a corpus accuracy in either direction. It supports exactly one claim: the detector is not fit to be the field value.

**Why the fill was never the real risk.** `isVerified` requires a `provenance.verification` record, so 10 of 787 entries actually serve `colorScheme`. Filling the 765 empty rows from detector output would be inert unless the migration also wrote verification records, and writing those from detector output is the laundering `verification-carry.ts` exists to prevent.

**Also fixed:** cohort re-derivation so a cherry-picked cohort is refused; report bound to its submission with decisions, confusion and status all derived; the answer key removed from the reviewer page; class balance added to the promotion floor; one canonicalisation repo-wide instead of two; the duplicated corpus path guard extracted after its copies had already diverged; a label-loss regression in the reviewer page; and the reviewer page's export paths made recoverable when the clipboard and blob download are both blocked.

**Known flaky, pre-existing:** `src/scripts/ui-browser.test.ts` passes 54/54 in isolation but can time out at 15s per test under parallel CPU contention. Unrelated to this branch.

**Deferred, with context in TODOS.md:** selector versioning and multi-reviewer support (prerequisites if the fill path is revived), the contaminated-entry exclusion, artifact version pinning, non-random-sample labelling, submission signing, and whether the migration has a consumer at all.

items.title: Add ONNX export and runtime support to Model API and predict CLI
items.body:
Closes #470.

Adds ONNX export and inference-runtime support to the Model API and the CLI. TensorRT is deliberately out of scope.

## What's here

- `Model.export("onnx", onnx_precision=...)` writes to `exports_onnx_dir()` as `{ckpt_stem}_{onnx_precision}.onnx`.
- `Model.from_dir(..., runtime="onnx", onnx_precision=...)` builds an ONNX Runtime session and rebinds `forward`, mirroring `compile()` so paths that call `get_loss_inputs_labeled` directly are covered.
- New `_runtime` attribute; `compile()` raises when `_runtime != "eager"`.
- `litpose export <model_dir> --runtime onnx --onnx-precision fp16`, plus `--runtime` / `--onnx-precision` on `litpose predict`. `--compile` with `--runtime onnx` is rejected in the CLI before the model is built, so the message matches the `compile()` guard rather than surfacing as a traceback.
- Provider guard raising when CUDA is available but `CUDAExecutionProvider` didn't load.
- Docs: `onnxruntime-gpu` installation section, ONNX section rewritten around the new API, `exports_onnx/` added to the model-directory reference. The TensorRT snippet was rewired to define its own variables, since it previously continued from the manual recipe that this PR removes.

## Three things I'd like your call on

**1. Context models.** The issue covers singleview and multiview dummy-input shapes. Context (MHCRNN) models need a third, `(1, T, 3, H, W)`. I added that branch with `T = 5`, matching the convention documented in `predict_frame`. But you may prefer `export()` to refuse context models outright rather than produce an export whose temporal behavior nobody has validated. Easy to switch to a `NotImplementedError`.

**2. `heatmap.py:211` registers `torch.tensor` results as constants in the trace.** Torch warns this "might cause the trace to be incorrect." The accuracy test passes at the config's resize dimensions, so it looks benign there — but that only covers the one resolution we tested. If that constant is shape-derived, an export reused at a different input resolution could be silently wrong. You know that head better than I do.

**3. CPU fallback.** The issue's `onnx_forward` hardcodes `device_type="cuda"`, but the provider guard only fires when `torch.cuda.is_available()`, so a CPU-only machine would build a session fine and then fail on first forward. I added a CPU branch. If ONNX should just be GPU-only, dropping it simplifies the code.

## Two corrections to the sketch

**`.half()` mutates in place.** `module_to_export = module_to_export.half()` returns `self`, so exporting fp16 from a live `Model` would leave `self.model` in half precision for every later eager call on that object. `export()` traces a `deepcopy` instead. Covered by `test_fp16_export_leaves_live_model_in_fp32`.

**`element_type=np.float32` is hardcoded.** An fp16 export expects fp16 input buffers. Input dtype is now read from the session's input metadata.

Two smaller ones: checkpoint resolution moved into a shared `_ckpt_stem()` with a `None` guard, so an untrained model directory raises the same `FileNotFoundError` as `_load()` rather than a `TypeError` from `Path(None)`; and `import onnxruntime` is deferred into `_attach_onnx_runtime()` so it stays optional for eager users.

## Testing

`tests/cli/`: 120 passed. `tests/api/test_model.py -k "Export or OnnxRuntime or Compile"`: 24 passed on a Tesla T4 (torch 2.8.0+cu128, onnxruntime 1.28.0, `CUDAExecutionProvider` confirmed active).

Covers export paths for both precisions, auto-selection with zero/one/multiple exports, export-vs-load checkpoint agreement, the lazy-load interaction, `compile()` rejection under `runtime="onnx"`, a mocked provider-guard test, and singleview + multiview. `test_onnx_matches_eager_predictions` confirms max pixel deviation under 0.1px against the eager model on real frames.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

Torch 2.9 makes the `dynamo=True` exporter the default and the current TorchScript path is deprecated. Works on 2.8, but worth its own issue.

items.title: perf: benchmark matrix + pipeline decomposition + Cantera baseline
items.body:
## Summary

A performance benchmark suite for ChemMechSim.jl. Builds on the compile/warm principle discovered during this work: the dominant perf cost for large mechanisms is one-time Julia JIT compilation of the MTK-generated Jacobian codegen, NOT the linear-solver choice.

### New scripts
- **`bench_matrix.jl`** — mechanism × linear-solver benchmark matrix (GRI30/FFCM2/Aramco × 5 direct sparse solvers: KLU/UMFPACK/Sparspak/MUMPS/Pardiso). Separates one-time compile (`compile_probe`) from per-solver warm solve + standalone linsolve micro-bench + trajectory accuracy vs reference. Repeats with median + IQR statistics.
- **`plot_bench.py`** — renders warm e2e time, compile-vs-N, and per-call linsolve figures (publication rcParams).
- **`plot_pipeline.py`** — stacked-bar pipeline decomposition (build / JIT compile / warm integrate) per mechanism.
- **`cantera_baseline.py`** — external baseline: Cantera cold/warm solve on the same GRI30 + Aramco problems.
- **`gri30_benchmark.jl`** — refactored from GRI30-only to multi-mech pipeline decomposition (build → cold → warm → jit_compile).

### Key findings

1. **JIT compilation dominates and scales with mechanism size** (gri30 8s → ffcm2 32s → aramco 569s), while warm solve stays small (~0.2 / 2.3 / 10s). The linear-solver choice is NOT the bottleneck.

2. **The earlier "KLU 35× slower" finding was a measurement artifact.** KLU ran first in the prior probe and paid the shared Jacobian-codegen compile (~422s); UMFPACK ran second (compile done, 12s). Fresh-process KLU (402s) ≈ UMFPACK (401s) — both pay the same compile.

3. **MUMPS is the fastest warm solver (3.6s on Aramco) but produces INCORRECT results** (T diverges by 1415K). The accuracy-vs-reference check catches this — without it, MUMPS would be misidentified as the winner.

4. **ChemMechSim warm (9.5s KLU) is competitive with Cantera (5.3s)** on Aramco — ~1.8× slower. The gap is entirely the cold-start JIT compile cost (569s vs Cantera's 5.4s), inherent to the symbolic-codegen approach.

5. **The optimization lever is opaque registered functions** (shrink the generated code → less to compile), not the linear solver. PLOG is already opaque; K_c and species sums are the next targets.

### Verification
- 5-solver × 3-mech × 5-repeat matrix run with accuracy check (MUMPS flagged incorrect).
- Cantera baseline: GRI30 + Aramco cold/warm timed.
- Pipeline benchmark: build/cold/warm/jit_compile for all 3 mechs.
- Smoke-tested on gri30 (all paths: e2e, micro-bench, accuracy, compile probe, metadata).

### Scope
`examples/perf/` + `Project.toml` (MUMPS, Pardiso, LinearSolve, Sparspak deps). No framework `src/` changes.

# 0020 Weak Topic Analytics

## Status

Accepted

## Context

StudyBot can generate quizzes and store graded attempts. Those attempts contain
the core signals needed for learning analytics: quiz topic, question count,
correct answers, incorrect answers, and attempt timestamps. The next step is to
turn that stored grading data into product intelligence that helps identify what
a learner should review next.

## Decision

Add course-scoped weak-topic analytics from quiz attempts.

The module includes:

- `GET /courses/{course_id}/weak-topics`
- topic-level aggregation by quiz topic
- total attempted topics, attempts, and questions
- per-topic:
  - attempt count

  - correct count
  - incorrect count

  - weakness score
  - average score percent
  - last attempted timestamp
- sorting by weakest topics first

No migration is required because this is read-only analytics over existing quiz
and quiz attempt tables.

StudyBot now closes a stronger study loop: generate a quiz, submit answers,
store graded attempts, and identify weak topics for review.

items.title: #62 Session summary + receipt computation
items.body:
## Summary
Implements the end-of-session receipt/summary (ADO #62; Technical Design §9) as a **pure, deterministic** function over a session's `CardResolution[]`.

`computeSessionSummary(input)` returns a typed `SessionSummary`:
- **completedCards / correctCards / accuracy** — `isCorrect` is the correctness source of truth, so a `timeout` resolution counts as incorrect (Tech §7). `accuracy = correctCards / completedCards`, defined as `0` for an empty session (no divide-by-zero).
- **totalElapsedMs** — sum of `elapsedMs` across resolved cards.
- **fastestCorrectCard** — the fastest **correct** card by `elapsedMs` (the field §9 names; `interactionElapsedMs` is the input-only measure). Ties resolve to **first occurrence**; absent when there were no correct cards.
- **categoryBreakdown** — per-`ChallengeCategory` `attempted` / `correct` / `medianElapsedMs`, in first-occurrence order. The card→category mapping is an **injected `categoryOf` lookup** (not a catalog import) so the core stays pure and testable; cards with no resolved category are still counted overall but omitted from the breakdown.
- **earnedExitBadge** — `completedCards >= MODE_DEFAULTS[mode].maxCards`. Duration-based early completion is the controller's concern and is intentionally out of scope for this pure function (documented `// DECISION:`).

**Positioning (Design §7):** session- and category-level performance only — no trait scores, no `hardestCategory`, no "weakest/strongest", no IQ/clinical/employment framing. **Template-agnostic** (CLAUDE.md §4/§6): aggregates only over the generic resolution + injected category, never narrows on `templateType`, never hard-codes the category list.

## Tests
`sessionSummary.test.ts` — 13 cases: accuracy across correct/incorrect/**timeout** mixes; fastest-correct selection incl. ignoring faster-but-incorrect cards, the no-correct case, and first-occurrence tie-break; category aggregation (odd/even median, undefined-category omission, first-occurrence order); exit-badge boundaries for **both** modes; edge cases (empty, all-timeouts, single card); and purity/determinism (no input mutation).

## Gate
`npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` — all green locally (**173 tests**).

References ADO #62.

items.body:
## Engine audit — confirmed defects fixed

A correctness audit of the lesson engine surfaced four real bugs, all stemming from the removal of the old graded **Vocab** phase (lessons are now 5 phases: Launch · Explore · Practice · Connect · Reflect).

### 1. Matching games graded as incorrect after a single wrong tap — HIGH
`matching-game.js` `finishGame()` only runs once **every** pair is matched (so completion always = success), but it reported `onComplete(pairs.length, attemptCount)`. The grader scores `correct === total`, so any completed game that had even one wrong tap was recorded **incorrect** — lowering accuracy, breaking the streak, and triggering remediation after a successful match. Now reports `(pairs.length, pairs.length)`; the wrong-attempt count still drives the star/efficiency message only.

### 2. Printable summary never showed Reflect answers — MEDIUM
`premium.js buildPrintableSummary` read the Reflect responses from legacy phase index **5**; the Reflect renderer saves them on phase **4**, so "One thing I learned" / "Confidence" always printed empty. Now reads phase 4.

### 3. Cover chips + teacher pacing labels shifted by one — MEDIUM
`PHASE_TIME_ESTIMATES` still carried a 6th "Vocab" entry while consumers label each row by index via `phaseName(0..4)` (5 entries). Every label below index 0 was mismatched (Vocab icon labeled "Explore", etc.) in the student cover chips and both teacher pacing guides. Dropped the stale entry.

### 4. "/6 phases" hardcoded — MEDIUM
Cover stats and the saved-student resume picker hardcoded `/6`, so a fully finished student showed `5/6` and never reached 100%. Now derived from `PHASE_TIME_ESTIMATES.length` (= 5).

items.title: fix(swa): evict overlap chunks using the actual extend boundary
items.body:
## Motivation

With overlap scheduling and `SWAChunkCache`, `maybe_evict_swa` currently derives the safe eviction boundary by subtracting the configured chunked-prefill size from the current prefix length. The actual preceding extend can be smaller than that configured size when the scheduler reduces a chunk to fit the available token budget.

For example, after a 4,096-token first chunk and a 1,536-token second chunk, the third scheduling pass sees a prefix length of 5,632. Subtracting the configured 4,096 produces 1,536, but the actual start of the in-flight second chunk is 4,096. The underestimated boundary can retain the first chunk and leave too few SWA slots for the next allocation, causing prefill to stop making progress.

## Modifications

- Track the real prefix length at the start of the most recently scheduled extend batch on each request.
- For the third and later overlap extend batches, evict only up to that recorded boundary while the preceding batch may still be in flight.
- Reset the recorded boundary when a request is retracted.
- Add focused tests for a reduced preceding chunk, fixed-size chunks, the first two protected overlap batches, non-overlap behavior, state recording, and retraction.

This change intentionally does not modify SWA pool sizing or admission accounting; those are separate from the incorrect overlap eviction boundary.

## Accuracy Tests

This only changes scheduler eviction metadata and does not change model arithmetic.

- `test_swa_chunk_eviction.py`: 6/6 passed on a clean `b31c4dfeb1` source tree.
- `test_prefill_adder.py`: 6/6 passed on the same source tree.
- qj5090 runtime smoke test: a 449-token Chinese prompt completed prefill and generated 31 tokens; strict UTF-8 validation passed with no replacement characters.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No throughput claim is made. The expected effect is to unblock affected variable-size overlap-prefill sequences without changing the fixed-size fast path.

## What changed

Implemented the **Daily validation/backtesting tracker for scoring engine accuracy** (backlog item 027).

### New files:
- `scripts/validation_tracker.py` — Core module with SQLite backend and optional Google Sheets integration
- `scripts/test_validation_tracker.py` — 34 tests covering SQLite schema, morning snapshots, EOD actuals, delta calculation, prediction correctness logic, report generation, Google Sheets fallback, CLI interface

### Features:
- **Morning run**: Records score_quote() output (score, decision, RSI, MACD, EMA positions, rationale) to SQLite + optional Google Sheets
- **EOD run**: Fetches actual closing prices via yfinance, computes delta_pct = (close - morning_close) / morning_close * 100
- **Prediction correctness**: score >= 60 AND price up → CORRECT; score < 60 AND price down → CORRECT; otherwise INCORRECT
- **Validation reports**: Per-symbol accuracy breakdown, win rates, average delta for correct vs incorrect predictions
- **Google Sheets integration**: Creates/updates "Agentic Trading Validation" sheet with proper columns (Date | Symbol | Score | Decision | RSI | MACD | EMA20_50_200 | Morning_Close | EOD_Close | Delta_Pct | Prediction_Correct | Accuracy_Flag)
- **SQLite fallback**: All data backed up to `data/validation.db` even if Google Sheets fails
- **Configurable tracked symbols**: Default [EREGL, ASELS, THYAO, SISE, ANHYT], overridable via DEFAULT_SYMBOLS constant
- **Trading day detection**: Skips weekends (BIST holidays extensible)

### Acceptance criteria met:
✅ New module `scripts/validation_tracker.py` with record_morning_score(), record_eod_actuals(), generate_validation_report()
✅ SQLite backend at data/validation.db with morning_snapshots, eod_actuals, weekly_summaries tables
✅ Google Sheets integration with proper columns and fallback to SQLite
✅ Handles BIST weekends gracefully (weekday check)
✅ Configurable tracked symbols list
✅ Graceful fallback: if Google Sheets write fails, logs to local SQLite

### Gate result: PASSED (196 tests, baseline updated from 160→193, then 196)

All four required fixes from Claude's review have been implemented:
1. ✅ EOD mode NameError fixed — `records` always bound before use; happy path calls record_eod_actuals(args.date, eod_prices, args.db)

4. ✅ Google Sheets path gated behind proper env vars (GOOGLE_SHEET_ID + API key) — removed auto-create-spreadsheet which fails without OAuth2

items.title: feat(self-review,peer-review): four reviewer axes the probes never asked about
items.body:
A high-impact medical-AI reject list was checked item by item against the 23 domain-probe
modules. Most of it was already owned somewhere. Four axes returned **zero hits across every
probe** — and three of those were not missing content, they were unreachable: the skills that
do the work already existed, and nothing on the reviewer side pointed at them.

| axis | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| standalone vs AI-assisted arm; automation bias | 0 hits in `diagnostic_accuracy.md` | **D12** |
| saliency-map faithfulness | `Grad-CAM` / `saliency` / `sanity check` = 0 hits in all 23 probes, while `/explainability` shipped the checks | **MD9** |
| uncertainty / OOD / abstention | `OOD` = 0; `abstention` only in `mllm_evaluation.md`; `/uncertainty-imaging` reachable only from `/design-study` | **MD10** |
| deployment feasibility & lifecycle | `dataset shift` / `inference time` = 0 hits | **MD11** |

### D12 — the assisted arm

`D5`/`D6` already covered fully-crossed designs, washout, Obuchowski–Rockette and the estimand.
What no probe asked: **which arm carries the claim**, and whether the assisted delta is split by
whether the AI was right. A pooled aided-minus-unaided delta can be positive while a stratum of
cases is made worse. Two radiology-specific findings ground this — incorrect AI BI-RADS
suggestions degraded reader performance with the largest effect in inexperienced readers
(Dratsch, *Radiology* 2023;307(4):e222176), and incorrect AI results reduced accuracy in a
multi-reader study (Bernstein, *Eur Radiol* 2023;33(11):8263–8269). Both verified against PubMed
before inclusion. D12 also requires the assistance paradigm (concurrent / second-reader / triage)
to be stated, since those measure different quantities and are not interchangeable.

### MD9–MD11 — scoped so they do not become a tax on every paper

- **MD9** asks for the Adebayo sanity checks and a cohort-level localisation metric before a
  saliency figure counts as evidence, and for attribution framing rather than "proof the model is
  correct". CLAIM 2024 item 31 already asks for explainability methods *and their validation*.
- **MD10** triggers **only under a clinical-use claim** — a plain retrospective accuracy study
  does not owe it. Requires measured coverage rather than an asserted interval, a held-out OOD
  set, and an abstention rate reported alongside retained-case performance.
- **MD11** is framed as **capping the claim, not invalidating the result** — a retrospective
  validation is not defective for lacking a latency number. AO4 keeps the claim; MD11 holds the
  operational facts that claim would need.

### Mechanics

- No new detector and no new CI gate: this is probe prose plus routing, so the gate count is
  unchanged at 238.
- Probe bodies edited in the **canonical** `peer-review` copy and vendored to `self-review` via
  `check_domain_probe_sync.py --sync`; both copies byte-identical.
- Range labels updated wherever the counts are quoted (`self-review`, `peer-review`,
  `model-validation`), and `metadata/distribution_files.json` regenerated.
- Local mirror **238/238**.

## summary

resets `region_counts` at the start of every `process()` call so the returned counts reflect the current frame's occupancy. previously the dict was only written when an object was inside a region, so after a frame with hits every later empty frame kept returning the old counts while the drawn label correctly showed 0. each named region now always appears in `region_counts`, with 0 when empty.

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary
🔄 This PR fixes `RegionCounter` so region totals are reset at the start of each frame, preventing counts from incorrectly carrying over between frames.

### 📊 Key Changes
- Added a reset step in `ultralytics/solutions/region_counter.py` inside `process()`.
- `self.region_counts` is now reinitialized for all configured counting regions before processing detections in each frame.
- This ensures each frame starts with a clean count state based on the defined region names.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ Prevents stale counts from previous frames from accumulating incorrectly.
- 📈 Improves accuracy and reliability of region-based counting results in videos and streams.
- 🛠️ Makes `RegionCounter` behavior more predictable for developers and end users.
- 🎥 Especially helpful for real-time analytics workflows where per-frame region counts need to reflect the current scene only.
